content:
emma: Heads-up — onboarding smoke tests failing after today's typegen regen. Auth e2e shows missing Authorization header in generated client requests.
jon: Which CI?
emma: job #4720. Failure snippet: 
```
FAIL e2e/auth.spec.ts
  Request did not include Authorization header
  at tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts:14:6
```
kevin: Any regendiff flagged?
publish-bot: publish-checker: regen mismatch detected for 'ts-sdk'. Files changed: generated/clients/sessionClient.ts. Semver impact: possible minor (behavioral).
maya: Hmm, we recently landed an OpenAPI example collapse that changed how the generator infers auth schemes. If examples that included bearer tokens are reordered out, generator now omits the default auth wrapper for some clients.
jon: So non-deterministic example ordering again? That keeps biting us.
emma: Yep. For onboarding sample-apps it's fatal because the example code relies on inferred auth wrapper to attach headers.
kevin: Short term we should patch sample-app to call client.withAuth(...) or set headers explicitly in the example so CI isn't implicitly depending on inferred behavior. I'll open a small PR.
maya: Long term: two fixes — 1) make typegen deterministic (stable sort examples + deterministic hashing), 2) stop inferring auth wrappers from example presence; require explicit "x-infer-auth": true annotation or fallback to no-op.
jon: Agree. Also note this is a behavioral change: aligning or changing defaults will require a semver minor and a changelog entry if we change ts-sdk to restore the wrapper. publishflow will block without it.
publish-bot: publish-checker: blocking reason — missing changelog for behavioral change in 'ts-sdk'.
emma: Plan: kevin patches sample-app to set Authorization explicitly to keep onboarding green; maya submits a codegen PR to add stable sort and an annotation gate; jon drafts a changelog in case we need to bump ts-sdk.
kevin: Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood/sample-apps/pull/623 — examples set explicit headers. Triggering CI.
maya: Codegen PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood/codegen/pull/845 — adds deterministic ordering for examples, a regen-hash test, and a feature flag that requires explicit auth inference. Local regen matches expected hash.
jon: Draft changelog: "Require explicit auth annotation for generated clients; align TypeScript SDK behavior to be explicit about Authorization header handling. This prevents accidental removal of auth wrappers when example ordering changes." Keep it non-technical but note behavioral impact.
emma: CI rerun: job 4720 rerun started.
publish-bot: regen-and-publish job started for thread 1788888888.
maya: Codegen branch CI passed, regen hashes stable.
publish-bot: publish-checker: regen-diff resolved on codegen branch.
jon: Decision on versioning: since this is changing default inference behavior (making auth inference opt-in), it's a behavior change — minor bump. But we can avoid a forced SDK release if we only change generator to require explicit annotations and leave current SDKs as-is; however, sample-apps should migrate to explicit headers. I'd prefer the conservative path: migrate sample-apps and release a minor that documents the opt-in.
kevin: Sample-app hotfix merged; onboarding tests passing locally. Pushing dependency updates to CI.
publish-bot: npm publish: ts-sdk@0.15.0 staging build created (not released) — changelog missing entry blocking permanent publish.
jon: I'll finalize the changelog entry describing the required explicit auth annotation for generated clients and link sample-app PR.
maya: Follow-ups: add a regen pipeline check that fails if examples are nondeterministic, and add a devex note encouraging explicit defaults in snippets to avoid reliance on inferred behavior.
emma: Thanks team — sample-app onboarding is green after the explicit header patch. We'll roll the minor release once changelog is in. Closing this thread and moving tasks to the DX board. :tada:
